title: Reporting Module — Scheduled Reports from Saved Dashboards
overview: Turn a saved dashboard into a report that is generated on a schedule and delivered by email. A person picks a report type (system, my reports, shared), picks a source dashboard, chooses what it covers (sites, devices or the whole portfolio, within what the source permits), picks PDF or Excel and — for PDF — which content it carries, sets a repeating day and time in a declared time zone or asks for it once, lists recipient email addresses, and switches it on. The platform builds the file, sends it, and records every run. Source: PRD-reporting-module-v1.pdf (2026-09-08, Mohamed Moanes, Draft) plus its companion PRD-reporting-module-v1-ANNEX.pdf, which authors the field dictionary (A), the screen state matrix (B) and the eleven failure states (C) — all three are design requirements authored nowhere else. This module has seven design surfaces, not four: the reporting setup page, the report editor, the run history, the entry point from a dashboard, and — named by the PRD as design work that is easy to forget is design work — the produced PDF, the produced Excel workbook, and the delivery email.

acceptance_criteria: Traces to PRD Requirement 4 (MUST/P0), proved by Checks 3 and 4

requirements.description: When the format is PDF, the editor offers a content choice of diagrams and tables, diagrams only, or tables only — and this control appears only for PDF.
acceptance_criteria: Traces to PRD Requirement 5 (MUST/P0) and ANNEX §A, proved by Check 3

requirements.description: The editor offers a schedule kind: repeating, or one-time.
acceptance_criteria: Traces to ANNEX §A, the schedule, and PRD Requirements 9 and 11

requirements.description: A repeating schedule has a required start-date field.
acceptance_criteria: Traces to ANNEX §A, the schedule

requirements.description: A repeating schedule has a required time-of-day field.
acceptance_criteria: Traces to ANNEX §A, the schedule, and PRD Requirement 9

requirements.description: A repeating schedule has a required time zone, stated on screen and never implicit.

requirements.description: A repeating schedule offers a repeat interval from a fixed set of three: daily, weekly, monthly. A monthly schedule whose start day does not exist in a given month runs on that month's last day.
acceptance_criteria: Decided at gate 1 by Mohamed Moanes (2026-09-14): a fixed set of daily / weekly / monthly. The ANNEX had left this [NEEDS INPUT].
No arbitrary interval builder, and no quarterly or yearly option in this release.
Decided at gate 1 round 3: a monthly report started on the 29th, 30th or 31st runs on the last day of any shorter month — it never skips a month.
The Start Date Field states this behaviour where a person setting a monthly schedule can see it, so a February run is not read as a defect.

requirements.description: The editor takes a recipient list of one or more email addresses, and at least one is required.
acceptance_criteria: Traces to PRD Requirement 13 (MUST/P0) and ANNEX §A, proved by Check 8

requirements.description: A recipient address need not belong to a platform user, and the editor does not require one to.
acceptance_criteria: Traces to PRD Requirement 13, proved by Check 8

Decided at gate 1 by Mohamed Moanes (2026-09-14): permitted, Owner and Admin only — Engineers do not hold it.
The recipient field therefore needs the inside/outside marker and an inline warning before an external address is accepted.

requirements.description: A generated file that exceeds the attachment ceiling fails the run visibly before sending, with a stated reason shown in run history, and the file is retained. There is no UI route to retrieve it — the run row says so plainly rather than implying the person can fetch it. No ceiling or size guidance is shown in the editor before the run.
acceptance_criteria: Never handed to a mail provider to drop
Traces to ANNEX §C #5 and §D, attachment ceiling
Decided at gate 1: the failure surfaces only as a failed run — the ceiling figure is still unsupplied, so no editor-side guidance can be written.

Decided at gate 1 round 3: retrieval of a retained file is a support or engineering action, not a UI affordance. The failure copy must not imply self-service retrieval, and download links remain an explicit non-goal.

requirements.description: Every quantity with kilo/mega/giga multiples is displayed scaled from its stored base unit, with the label derived from the value — on screen and inside the PDF and Excel file.

requirements.description: The produced PDF is recognizably the dashboard it came from — same ordering, same grouping, legible, nothing cut off.

requirements.description: Every action in this module is gated on a named privilege rather than a role name, so a client creating or renaming roles later breaks nothing.

requirements.description: Report definitions, generated files and run history are scoped to one client account and unreadable from another by any route.

requirements.description: The four screen surfaces — Reporting Setup Page, Report Editor, Run History, Dashboard Entry Point — meet WCAG 2.2 AA. The produced PDF and the delivery email are out of scope for accessibility in this release.
acceptance_criteria: Decided at gate 1 by Mohamed Moanes (2026-09-14). The ANNEX had recorded this as [NEEDS INPUT] with no bar given.
Explicitly excludes tagged-PDF output, which is a renderer requirement rather than a styling one.
Applies to contrast, focus order, and the screen-reader consequences of the hidden-not-disabled rule (REQ-39).

screens.name: Reporting setup page

required_elements: Three type tabs: system / my reports / shared
Count badge per tab
Report list with selectable columns
Filter control
Search field
Pager and page-size selector
"Showing X of Y" counter

Per-row "source unavailable" marker

Open a tab with no reports -> use the empty-state affordance to create one

Source dashboard picker — exactly one, shown first
Coverage kind: sites / devices / whole portfolio
Coverage scope picker, constrained by the source
Period field, defaulted from the source
Output format: PDF or Excel
PDF content choice: diagrams and tables / diagrams only / tables only
Schedule kind: repeating or one-time
Start date, time of day, time zone, repeat interval
Recipient list with inside/outside-organization marking
Active switch, off by default
Generate-once action
Empty state — source picker only
Loading state — coverage options visibly pending
Forbidden state — absent controls, no layout gap
Error state — save failure keeps entered values
Partial-data state — resolved coverage shown, unresolved named
user_flows: Pick a type -> pick a report -> pick a source dashboard -> choose coverage -> choose PDF or Excel and its content -> set a day, time and time zone -> enter addresses -> switch it on
Define a report -> generate it once on demand without scheduling it

screens.name: Run history
screens.description: Per report: every run, what it covered, the file it produced, who received it, and whether it worked.
required_elements: Run rows: ran-at, coverage as run, file reference, recipients as sent, outcome
Newest-first ordering with paging
Running state for a mid-flight run
Failure reason on a failed run
Inactive-after-retries state with creator notification
Delivered-with-failures state naming the bounced addresses
Empty state — never run, stated plainly
Forbidden state — absent without the read-history privilege
Error state that does not block the report
user_flows: Open a report -> open its run history -> find out that last night's run did not send, and why

screens.name: Way in from a dashboard
screens.description: "Make a report from this" on a dashboard, carrying the dashboard in as the pre-chosen source.
required_elements: Entry-point affordance on a dashboard
Inline loading
Hidden where the create privilege is absent
Error fallback to the setup page with the source pre-chosen
user_flows: Look at a dashboard -> make a report from it -> land in the editor with the source already set

screens.name: The produced PDF
screens.description: A design surface, not an export side effect: it must be recognizably the dashboard it came from, in three content variants.
required_elements: Header naming the report, source dashboard, period, coverage and declared authority
Diagrams-and-tables variant
Diagrams-only variant
Tables-only variant
Quantities scaled from base unit with derived labels
No-readings statement instead of an empty page
Named placeholder for a panel that could not render
user_flows: A recipient opens the attachment and agrees it is the dashboard it came from

screens.name: The produced Excel workbook
screens.description: One sheet per panel, with the values behind every chart — the asymmetric twin of the PDF.
required_elements: One sheet per dashboard panel
Series values behind diagram panels
Quantities scaled from base unit with derived labels
No-readings sheet instead of an empty sheet
Sheet naming the problem for an unresolvable panel
user_flows: A recipient opens the workbook and works with the numbers behind the charts

screens.name: The delivery email
screens.description: The fifth surface the PRD insists is design work: what arrives in the inbox of somebody who may not be a Sand user at all.
required_elements: Subject and body identifying the report, its source, period and coverage
The attachment
No partial email on a failed run
user_flows: A recipient who has no Sand account receives the file and can tell what it is

use_cases: As an Asset Manager, have last week's portfolio summary in my inbox on Monday without opening Sand.
As an O&M Manager, send the same site report to the same three people weekly and stop rebuilding it.
As somebody in the client's Technical Office, produce one report now, for one site, with no schedule.
As an Owner or Admin, stop a shared report going to the wrong people without hunting for its author.
As anybody who set one up, find out that last night's report did not send, and why.
constraints: Out of scope: reports built on customer-defined formulas (the Formula Builder is postponed).
Out of scope: any mobile surface.
Out of scope: new report content — charts, figures or KPIs the platform cannot already show. Every report is a dashboard snapshot.
Out of scope: report building outside a dashboard. If a person wants what no dashboard shows, they build the dashboard first.
Out of scope: any delivery route other than email — no in-platform inbox, download links or file storage surface.
Out of scope: billing documents and invoices.
Out of scope: output formats other than PDF and Excel.
Out of scope: recipient-side permission checks — recipients are email addresses, not platform users, so there is nobody to check. The PRD names this the largest risk in the document.
Out of scope: editing or annotating a generated file.
Depends on the Admin Module (in user acceptance testing) — without it the private and shared report types are meaningless.
Depends on the dashboard builders (in user acceptance testing) — without them there are no custom sources.
Depends on a working email route, which is in the pipeline with no date — nothing delivers without it.
Every requirement is written against a privilege, never a role name, because a later Admin Module release lets a client define its own roles.
Where a person lacks authority the control is hidden, not greyed out, and the layout leaves no hole — the same rule the Admin Module and the dashboards use.
No delivery date, target quarter or committed date appears in the PRD, by the Product Manager's deliberate decision.

unverified_prd_claims.claim: "Where a person lacks a privilege the control is hidden, not greyed out, and the layout leaves no hole where it would have been" — described as "the same rule the Admin Module and the dashboards use" (PRD Requirement 24, PRD §5).

"The report lists support choosing columns, filtering, searching and paging, with a page-size selector, a 'showing X of Y' counter, and count badges on the three tabs" — sourced to the Admin PRD, i.e. asserted to be an existing shipped list pattern (PRD Requirement 26).

"The manual report creation that already shipped is unchanged by this release" — asserts an existing, shipped manual reporting UI in SandGen (PRD Requirement 27; ANNEX §H: G1.3 Reporting Shipped, "users can generate reports in SandGen").
"SandGen default dashboards — Shipped 2026-08" — asserts system default dashboards already exist as sources (ANNEX §H).

"The Admin Module and the dashboard builders are in user acceptance testing, not released" — taken from the brief and the Product Manager without independent confirmation; the PRD notes 09_shipped-state.md still records both as in progress (PRD Assumptions).
"Sand has a mail abstraction but no delivered email route" — taken from PRD-notification-center-v5 and flagged by the PRD itself as a dependency to confirm, not a fact to build on (PRD Assumptions).

"Rendering reads the same document-canvas-element chain the screen renders from. The PDF and the screen then agree by construction rather than by a second layout implementation" — asserts an existing composition chain specified by PRD-customizable-dashboards-v2 (ANNEX §E).
"Sites, devices and portfolio are Scope" — asserts an existing polymorphic Scope hierarchy that coverage selection reuses rather than introduces (ANNEX §E, PRD §7).

"The Admin Module's four roles — Owner, Admin, Engineer, Technician" — asserts the live role set the permission table is built on, against eight commercial role names in 01_company-and-product-overview.md, with no mapping proposed (PRD §5).

The PRD's Assumptions and ANNEX §K state outright that the grounding documents are dated snapshots — 08_sand-fit-architecture-digest.md (2026-08-02) and two September-2025 commercial files — and that "the live repository and the current price sheet are the final authority, not this document."
